directions.name: Gallery White
directions.summary: Pure white and black, so the work is the only color.
directions.curation: The gallery wall: no chroma at all, for brands whose product or imagery must carry every color.

reasoning.claim: Black reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Gallery White, the maximum separation for type.
With no brand color, photography and product supply the identity, which suits fashion and galleries.

directions.watch_out: Without strong imagery it looks unfinished.
avoid: Do not add an accent color to "liven it up".

directions.name: Atelier Black
directions.summary: Black ground, white type and nothing else: severe, restrained and exclusive.
directions.curation: The tasteful default for luxury: black, or black and white, without a metallic cue. Owner's taste rule, recorded in contexts/conventions.json.

reasoning.claim: Paper White reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Atelier Black, so type is crisp at any size.
Black and white carries exclusivity and restraint on its own, so the product and photography are the only color.

directions.watch_out: Full black pages are heavy for long reading. Use white panels for editorial text and product details.
do: Use generous space and precise type.
avoid: Do not add gold to signal luxury.
Do not soften the black to gray.

directions.name: Black Tie
directions.summary: Black and white with a hairline of flat old gold: the conventional premium cue, kept scarce.
directions.curation: Included so the conventional black-and-gold language is available, done with restraint: a muted flat gold at 3% of the area. Flagged as a cliché risk in contexts/conventions.json.

reasoning.claim: Old Gold holds 3% of the declared area and reaches {ratio:accent/ground} on Evening Black, so it works as rules and small marks.
Gold reads as conventional premium signalling. Kept flat and scarce it adds ceremony; used more, it turns generic.

directions.watch_out: Gold on black is the most common premium cliché. Never use metallic gradients, and keep gold to hairlines and small marks.
do: Keep Old Gold to hairlines, numerals and one mark.
avoid: Do not use foil or metallic gradients on screen.
Do not set body text in gold.

directions.name: Burgundy Silk
directions.summary: A deep burgundy ground with ecru: rich, quiet and tactile.
directions.curation: Built on luxury textiles: a deep wine ground with an undyed-fabric figure, without metallic cues.

reasoning.claim: Ecru reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Burgundy, so the ground can carry all type.
A deep muted ground reads as rich rather than loud, which suits jewelry and leather.

directions.watch_out: Burgundy grounds can darken product photography. Present products on ecru panels.
do: Use Ecru panels behind product shots.
avoid: Do not add gold foil effects on screen.

directions.name: Grey Marl and Safety Orange
directions.summary: Grey marl jersey with hard safety-orange blocks and black type.
directions.curation: Borrowed from training gear and workwear: grey marl fabric with a high-visibility orange used as graphic blocks.

reasoning.claim: Safety Orange reaches only {ratio:figure/ground} on Grey Marl, so it works as blocks and tags while type stays in the derived dark neutral.
A utility color on athletic grey carries a practical, physical attitude that suits sportswear and streetwear.

directions.watch_out: Orange text on grey is unreadable. Every word goes in the dark text color.
directions.figure_role: Graphic blocks, tags and the mark
do: Use Safety Orange as flat blocks and tags.
avoid: Do not set text in Safety Orange.

directions.name: Butter and Chocolate
directions.summary: A soft butter-yellow ground with chocolate brown: warm, retro and friendly.
directions.curation: A two-tone lifestyle identity with a tinted ground, warm without being sweet.

reasoning.claim: Chocolate reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Butter Yellow, so it carries all text.
A yellow ground with brown type recalls mid-century print and feels warm and unpretentious.

directions.watch_out: Yellow grounds shift a lot between screens. Check on several devices.
do: Use Butter Yellow as the main field.
avoid: Do not pair it with pastel pink.

directions.name: Bare Skin
directions.summary: Shell white and a soft nude rose, with type in the derived text color.
directions.curation: A low-contrast skin-tone pair for products about the skin itself, with text carried by a darker derived neutral.

reasoning.claim: Nude Rose reaches only {ratio:figure/ground} on Shell, so it is used for fields and panels, never for text.
A low-contrast, skin-toned pair feels gentle and close, which suits skincare.

directions.watch_out: Nude tones represent only some skin tones. Check how the palette sits beside a diverse range of models.
directions.figure_role: Color fields, packaging panels and illustration
do: Use Nude Rose for large fields and packaging.
avoid: Do not set any text in Nude Rose.

directions.name: Lipstick
directions.summary: A blush white with a pure lipstick red.
directions.curation: A single product-true red on a barely tinted white: the product color is the brand color.

reasoning.claim: Lipstick Red reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Blush White, so it can carry headlines and links.
One saturated red on white is confident and immediately readable.

directions.watch_out: A strong red is hard to use for errors as well. Define a separate error color.
directions.figure_role: Mark, headlines and calls to action
do: Use Lipstick Red for the mark and one action per view.
avoid: Do not add a second saturated hue.

directions.name: Lab Clean
directions.summary: Cool white and slate with a small aqua accent: clinical but not cold.
directions.curation: A clinical neutral pair with one cool accent, for science-led skincare and medical products.

reasoning.claim: Slate reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Lab White, so all reading text can use it.
Aqua holds 4% of the declared area, so it marks without coloring the whole brand.

directions.watch_out: Aqua is decorative on white. Do not use it for anything that must be read.
do: Use Aqua for small illustrations and markers.
avoid: Do not set text or icons in Aqua.
